1.5 cups coarse bulgur: 2 long green peppers, 1 red pepper
Fry the onion and peppers in oil for 5 minutes.
Add the tomato paste and stir for 1 minute.
Add the bulgur and toast for 2 minutes.
Add the water and salt and cook for 15 minutes.
Don’t wash the bulgur; the pilaf will turn mushy.
Rice pilaf with peas
1.5 cups baldo rice
Soak the rice in hot salted water for 20 minutes and wash until the starch is gone.
Toast the rice in the fats for 4 minutes.
Add the peas, water and salt.
Cook over low heat for 15 minutes.
Let rest for 15 minutes.
Washing the rice well gives fluffy, separate grains.
Quinoa pilaf with tomato
1.5 cups quinoa
1 dessert spoon salt, 1 teaspoon thyme
Rinse the quinoa thoroughly in a fine sieve.
Fry the onion in oil, add the tomato and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the quinoa and stir for 1 minute.
Add the water, salt and thyme and cook for 15 minutes.
Let rest for 5 minutes and fluff with a fork.
When quinoa is cooked, a white ring appears around each grain.
Orzo pilaf with carrots
1.5 cups orzo
2.5 cups hot chicken stock or water
Toast the orzo in butter for 4 minutes until golden.
Add the carrot and stir for 2 minutes.
Add the hot water and salt.
Cook over low heat for 12 minutes.
Stir constantly while toasting the orzo; it burns quickly.
Bulgur pilaf with spinach
1.5 cups bulgur
Add the bulgur and stir for 2 minutes.
Add the water and salt and cook for 10 minutes.
Spread the chopped spinach on top, put the lid on and cook for 5 more minutes.
Stir and let rest for 10 minutes.
Added in the last 5 minutes, spinach keeps its colour.
Couscous pilaf with corn
1.5 cups couscous
1 cup corn
1.5 cups hot chicken stock or water
Sauté the onion in butter for 3 minutes, then the carrot for 4 minutes.
Add the corn and stir for 2 minutes.
Add the couscous and toast for 1 minute.
Add the hot water, salt and pepper, turn off the heat and leave covered for 10 minutes.
Fluff with a fork and serve.
Couscous isn’t cooked but steeped; don’t forget to turn off the heat.
Serve hot alongside chicken or köfte.
Bulgur pilaf with eggplant
1 dessert spoon salt, half a teaspoon black pepper
Dice the eggplants, soak in salted water for 15 minutes and pat dry.
Fry the eggplants in 2 tablespoons of oil and set aside.
Cook the onion and tomato in the remaining oil and add the bulgur.
Add the water and salt, cook for 12 minutes and add the eggplant.
Soaking eggplant in salted water reduces bitterness and oil absorption.
Buckwheat pilaf with lentils
Pre-boil the lentils for 15 minutes and drain.
Add the buckwheat and lentils and stir for 2 minutes.
Add the water, salt and cumin and cook for 15 minutes.
A pilaf rich in plant protein.
Rice pilaf with zucchini
1.5 cups rice
1 zucchini (diced)
Soak and wash the rice.
Sauté the zucchini in butter for 3 minutes.
Add the rice and toast for 3 minutes.
Cook with the water and salt for 15 minutes.
Add the dill and let it rest.
Don’t overcook the zucchini; it falls apart.
Bulgur pilaf with leeks
Slice the leek into thin rings and dice the carrot.
Sauté in oil for 6 minutes and add the tomato paste.
Wash the grit from between the leek layers in plenty of water.
Chicken and mushroom sauté
400 g chicken breast (diced)
1 onion (sliced)
1 green pepper (rings)
1 tomato (diced)
Half a tea glass hot water
Heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a wide pan over high heat; sauté the chicken for 6–7 minutes until it releases and reabsorbs its juices and browns lightly, then transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining oil to the same pan and cook the mushrooms over high heat for 5 minutes until the liquid evaporates and they brown.
Add the onion and pepper and sauté for 3 more minutes.
Add the tomato paste and fry for 1 minute, then add the tomato and hot water.
Return the chicken to the pan; season with salt, pepper and thyme and cook over low heat for 5 minutes.
Make sure the chicken is no longer pink inside and serve hot.
Cooking the chicken and mushrooms separately lets both brown; together they would stew.
Serve with rice pilaf or bulgur pilaf.
Chicken sauté in curry sauce
600 g chicken breast (cubed)
1 dessert spoon grated ginger
1 tablespoon curry powder
1 cup coconut milk or cream
2 tablespoons vegetable oil
Toss the chicken with salt and curry.
Sear the chicken in oil over high heat for 6–7 minutes and remove.
In the same pan, sauté the onion, garlic, ginger and pepper for 5 minutes.
Return the chicken and pour in the coconut milk.
Cook over low heat for 10 minutes until the sauce thickens and the chicken is cooked through.
Frying the curry in oil for 30 seconds releases its aroma.
Serve hot with basmati rice.
Creamy chicken with broccoli
450 g chicken breast (strips)
300 g broccoli (small florets)
2 tablespoons grated kashar
Blanch the broccoli in salted boiling water for 3 minutes, plunge into cold water and drain.
Sauté the chicken in olive oil over high heat for 6 minutes and transfer to a plate.
Melt the butter in the same pan; fry the onion and garlic for 3 minutes.
Add the flour and fry for 1 minute, gradually whisk in the milk and stir for 3 minutes until thick.
Add the chicken and broccoli to the sauce; season with salt and pepper and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the kashar, remove from the heat once melted and serve.
Briefly blanching the broccoli first keeps its colour bright.
Serve hot with pasta or rice pilaf.
Keeps for 2 days in the fridge; add a little milk when reheating.
Lemon chicken with leeks
450 g chicken breast (diced)
2 leeks (rings)
1 carrot (rounds)
Wash the leeks and clean off all the grit.
